n: Jesus now speaks to the crowds and his disciples about the religious leaders. This is his final public teaching in the temple.

f.w: to the multitude, and to his disciples

n: The scribes and Pharisees act as official teachers of the law of Moses, as though seated in his chair.

f.g: A seat of teaching authority; ancient synagogues had a stone chair by this name.

n: So far as they teach the law, listen to them — but don’t copy their behavior, because they don’t practice what they preach.
They pile heavy religious rules on people but won’t lift a finger to help them carry the load.

f.g: Hard to carry.

n: Their religion is a performance. They make their scripture boxes extra wide and their tassels extra long to look especially devout.

f.g: Small leather boxes holding scripture passages, strapped to the forehead and arm during prayer.
The tassels on cloak corners commanded in the law.

n: They love the honored seats at banquets and the front seats in synagogues.

f.g: The places of honor at the table.
Synagogue seats facing the congregation.

n: They enjoy respectful public greetings and being called “Rabbi.”

f.g: Hebrew “my great one” — a title of honor for a teacher.

n: Disciples shouldn’t seek such titles. Christ is their one Teacher, and they are all equals.
Don’t give anyone the ultimate honor that belongs only to our Father in Heaven. Jesus targets status-seeking, not normal respect for parents.

f.w: one is your Father, which is in heaven

n: Christ alone is the final guide and leader.

f.g: Greek kathēgētēs — instructor, guide, leader.

n: Greatness in Christ’s kingdom is measured by service.
God reverses human pride: the self-promoting will be humbled, and the humble lifted up.

f.g: abased = brought low, humbled.

f.w: he that shall humble himself shall be exalted

n: The first of a series of woes. They shut the door of God’s kingdom — refusing to enter themselves and blocking others who want to.

f.g: An expression of grief and warning of judgment — the opposite of “blessed.”

f.w: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven

n: They cheat vulnerable widows out of their homes while making a show of long prayers. Their punishment will be greater. (Many ancient manuscripts lack this verse; Mark 12:40 has it.)

f.g: For show, as a cover.

n: They travel everywhere to win a single convert, then make that convert even more misguided than themselves.

f.g: compass = travel around.
A Gentile convert to Judaism.

n: They taught that oaths by the temple didn’t bind, but oaths by its gold did — clever loopholes for lying.

f.g: He is bound by his oath.

n: Which is greater — the gold, or the temple that makes the gold holy?

f.g: sanctify = make holy, set apart for God.

n: They made the same hair-splitting distinction between swearing by the altar and by the offering on it.

f.w: the gift that is upon it
f.g: The sacrifice offered on the altar.

n: The altar is what makes the gift holy. Their reasoning was upside down.

f.w: the altar that sanctifieth the gift

n: An oath by the altar includes everything on it.

f.w: sweareth by it, and by all things thereon
f.g: There is no loophole.

n: An oath by the temple is ultimately an oath by God, who dwells there.
And swearing by heaven is swearing by God himself. Every oath involves God; honesty can’t be dodged.
They carefully tithe tiny garden herbs but neglect the weightier things — justice, mercy, faithfulness. Jesus says do both, but don’t lose the heart of the law.

f.g: Small kitchen herbs and spices; anise is likely dill.
judgment = justice; faith = faithfulness.

n: A comic picture: carefully straining a tiny gnat out of a drink while gulping down a whole camel. Both were unclean animals.

f.g: Strain out a gnat — people filtered wine through cloth to avoid swallowing unclean insects.

n: They clean the outside of cups and dishes but leave the inside full of greed and self-indulgence.

f.g: Robbery and lack of self-control.

n: Clean the inside first; a clean heart leads to genuinely clean outward conduct.

f.w: cleanse first that which is within

n: They’re like whitewashed tombs: bright and clean on the outside, full of decay inside. Tombs were whitewashed so people wouldn’t accidentally touch them and become unclean.

f.g: Tombs painted with lime, especially before Passover, to mark them.

n: Likewise, they look righteous to others but are full of hypocrisy and sin inside.
They build and decorate monuments to the prophets their ancestors killed.

f.g: Decorate the tombs.

n: They claim they would never have joined in killing the prophets.

f.g: Sharers, accomplices.

n: But by calling them “our fathers,” they admit their descent — and their actions show they share the same spirit.

f.g: You testify against yourselves.

n: Bitter irony: go ahead and finish what your ancestors started — a reference to the plot to kill Jesus.

f.w: Fill ye up then the measure
f.g: Complete the full amount of their guilt.

n: Jesus uses John the Baptist’s harsh words: snakes, offspring of vipers. How will they escape judgment?

f.g: Condemnation to Gehenna.

n: Jesus will send more messengers — prophets, wise men, and teachers — and they too will be persecuted and killed.
This generation will bear accountability for all the righteous blood shed, from the first murder (Abel) to Zacharias — the first and last murders in the Hebrew Bible’s order.

f.g: Most likely the priest Zechariah stoned in the temple court (2 Chronicles is last in the Hebrew Bible); Joseph Smith taught it referred to John the Baptist’s father.

n: Judgment will fall on this very generation — fulfilled when Rome destroyed Jerusalem and the temple in AD 70.
Jesus’s anger turns to heartbreak. Like a mother hen sheltering chicks, he longed to gather and protect Jerusalem’s people — but they refused.

f.w: as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings

n: Their “house” — likely the temple and the city — will be left abandoned and desolate.

f.w: your house is left unto you desolate

n: They won’t see him again until they welcome him with the words of Psalm 118 — pointing ahead to his Second Coming, when Israel will recognize him.

f.w: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord
